newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs surge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs surge.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials rallied on a spurt of shortcovering ahead of the weekend on Friday while the Midcontinent stayed aloft on continued concerns of supply, players said.

New York Harbor remained quiet as players watched the surge in NYMEX gasoline as dealers interpreted refinery disruptions in Europe as detaining cargoes that were expected to appear in the Horbor in the coming weeks.
September gasoline futures closed up 2.27 cents at 65.07 cents a gallon, with heating oil up 0.37 at 56.57. September crude closed up 14 cents at $20.28 a barrel.
U.S. GULF
Prompt conventional M1 gasoline differentials jumped higher by late Friday, with traders reporting a deal done at 2.25 cents over the September contract, a gain of about 1.75 cents on the day.
Market watchers pointed to brisk short covering by one Gulf Coast trader as a key reason for the gains.
Prompt reformulated A2 gasoline differentials also firmed by late day, with barrels talked slightly above 6.00 cents over the September NYMEX, or about 4.00 cents over the prompt M1-grade.
However, the strength in the prompt barrels did not affect the any-month M1 gasoline, traders said, which stood near 2.75 cents under the September futures.

Distillate markets showed little movement in the Gulf Friday, with prompt heating oil offered at 2.40 cents under the September NYMEX and prompt low sulphur diesel offered at 1.40 cents under the futures.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent gasoline markets remained firm Friday afternoon although activity slackened as players took off for the weekend. Group Three unleaded differentials stayed aloft at 6.50/6.75 cents above September NYMEX futures, about a quarter cent down from this morning.

Group Three unleaded has firmed more than two cents this week as rising prices in the U.S. Gulf cut back on volumes through the pipeline to the Midwest. Traders said there is a low 18-days worth of supply in the Williams Pipeline.
Chicago market unleaded differentials also held at 6.75/7.00 cents over the print, a range that was bid up on Thursday due to heavy refinery buying.
Players said there was some selling on low sulphur diesel in Chicago at 0.75 cents under the print. Group Three low sulphur was talked 2.25/2.50 cents.
NEW YORK HARBOR
New York Harbor gasoline differentials were slightly weaker due to very quiet activity and the sharp rise on NYMEX gasoline futures.
Prompt M2-grade conventional unleaded gasoline differentials were done at 2.60 cents over the screen, with the range at 2.40/2.65 cents. Any months were about even to a penny under the print.
Prompt A2 reformulated northern grade was also traded at 7.50 cents over the print, unchanged from this morning. Barrels for delivery by Aug 10 were done at 5.60 cents over the screen.

Traders expressed some concern over the continued strength in prices of MTBE, an A2 gasoline additive. Production problems and several turnarounds scheduled for September are expected to keep a floor under late August and September MTBE values, unlike previously expected.
